content.title: What is Python?
content.body:
Python is a programming language — a way of writing instructions that computers can understand.

It was created by a programmer named Guido van Rossum. The name came from Monty Python, a British comedy group — not the snake.

Today, Python is one of the most widely used programming languages in the world. Beginners use it to learn programming, and professionals use it to build real software.

content.title: Python was designed to be readable
content.body:
One reason Python is popular for learning is that the code is designed to be readable and easier for humans to understand.

Python avoids a lot of extra symbols and complicated formatting. The rules are still important — spelling, punctuation, and spacing can matter — but the code is often easier to follow than many other programming languages.

content.title: Python is used for real projects
content.body:
Python is used for many different kinds of technology:

• Building websites and apps
• Analysing data and graphs
• Automating repetitive tasks
• Scientific and space research
• Creating games and tools
• AI and machine learning

Python isn't just a "practice" language. It's a real tool used by programmers all over the world.

content.title: Your first look at Python
content.body:
print("Hello! What's your name?")

name = "Alex"
print("Nice to meet you,", name)

score = 0
score = score + 10

print("Your score is:", score)

content.title: You don't need to understand everything yet
content.body:
That code might look unfamiliar right now — and that's completely normal.

Over the next lessons, you'll learn what each line means step by step:

• How to print text
• How variables store information
• How programs remember and update values

For now, just notice that Python code is readable and structured.

Next, you'll start by learning how to print text to the screen.

quiz.question: Python was named after the snake.
quiz.explanation: Correct. Python was named after Monty Python, a British comedy group.

quiz.question: Why do many beginners start with Python?

options.text: Because it was the first programming language ever made
Because Python code is designed to be readable
Because it only works for games

quiz.explanation: Python was designed to be readable and easier for humans to understand.

quiz.question: Which of these is something Python is commonly used for?
quiz.explanation: Python is commonly used for websites, data analysis, automation, AI, science, and many other kinds of software.

quiz.question:
What does this line of Python code do?

print("Hello")

options.text: Shows the word Hello on the screen

quiz.explanation: The print command displays text on the screen.
